title: Mnestiq: forensic evidence for AI agents
excerpt: Trace a network connection back to the AI agent step that made it, and prove the record wasn't altered. Open source, Apache-2.0.
content_html:
Open source · forensic evidence for AI agents

Trace a network connection back to the AI agent step that made it.

Mnestiq records what your agents saw, decided and did as signed, tamper-evident evidence. When something goes wrong, you can name the run, the step, the input that drove it and who approved it, and prove the record wasn't altered afterwards.

pip install mnestiq

v1.1.1 · Apache-2.0 · Python 3.10+ · Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and compatible APIs · PyPI

One log line, tracedexample

  1. Firewall10.0.4.17:53120 → 198.51.100.9:25 · 48 KB · no agent identity
  2. Mnestiqagent support-bot · run f48cccfa · step 6 · sandbox container:a91f02 · operator acme-helpdesk
  3. Causeuntrusted input at step 4 (web, via fetch_page) → model requested send_email → approved by policy:email-auto-approve
  4. Evidencesealed by checkpoint · signer ed25519:6bec5262… (pinned) · corroborated by vpc-flow.log, conn.log

The gap

Your logs see connections. Your traces see prompts. Nothing connects them.

A firewall alert: a host that runs AI agents sent 48 KB to an outside mail server on port 25. The responder now has three questions, and today's tools answer none of them.

Network logs

10.0.4.17:53120 → 198.51.100.9:25 · 48 KB

An address, a port and a byte count. No agent, run or step.

nothing
links them

Agent traces

model call → tool call: send_email

Prompts and tool calls. No address, port or connection.

Q1

Which agent did this?

Firewall and flow logs show an IP and a port. They don't know about agents, runs or steps.

Q2

Why did it do it?

Was the instruction from the user, or from a web page, a document or another agent? That has to be captured when it happens, not reconstructed later.

Q3

Can we prove it?

Ordinary logs can be edited by anyone with write access. Evidence for a post-mortem, an insurer or a regulator needs to show it wasn't.

How it works

Record, verify, investigate.

01 · Record

A flight recorder in the agent

Records agents built on Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible models in a few lines. Built to fail safely: if recording fails, the agent keeps running.

  • Every piece of model input tagged by source: user, web, tool output, retrieved document, another agent
  • Tool calls, approvals and effective permissions
  • Every outbound connection, with run identity headers and the local address and port

usersystem webtool outputretrieved documentanother agent

Marked sources are treated as untrusted by the detection rules.

Quick startPython

# $ pip install "mnestiq[anthropic]"
# $ mnestiq keygen --out keys
# Instrument an existing agent. Your agent code doesn't change.
import anthropic
from mnestiq import FileSink, Recorder
from mnestiq.egress import instrument_egress
from mnestiq.integrations.anthropic import instrument_anthropic
from mnestiq.keys import load_private_key

recorder = Recorder(FileSink("evidence.jsonl"), agent_id="support-bot",
                    signing_key=load_private_key("keys/signing.key"))
client = instrument_anthropic(anthropic.Anthropic(), recorder)
instrument_egress()   # stamp and record outbound connections during runs

with recorder.run():
    ...                # your agent, as it is today
recorder.close()       # signs the last checkpoint: verify needs it

# Later: $ mnestiq verify evidence.jsonl --trusted-key keys/signing.pub

02 · Verify

Tamper-evident by construction

Records are hash-chained and sealed by Ed25519-signed Merkle checkpoints.

  • Edits, deletions, insertions and reordering fail verification
  • Pin the recorder's key, and a re-signed forgery is rejected
  • Redact prompts and customer data before sharing, and the proof still holds

recordhash of the record before

recordhash of the record before

Signed checkpointMerkle root of the records it covers · Ed25519 signature

Change, remove, add or reorder a record and the hashes stop matching what was signed.

03 · Investigate

From a log line to a cause

Join agent evidence with the infrastructure logs you already collect.

  • VPC flow logs, Zeek and proxy logs linked to the exact agent step, with a confidence score
  • The untrusted input that preceded an action, and who approved it
  • Traffic from agent hosts that no recorded step explains

Every record above is sealed by a signed checkpoint.

When someone edits the record

Built for the person holding the incident.

What the responder gets

The run, the step, the input and the approval.

The same evidence file answers the three questions: which agent, why, and whether the record can be shown to be unaltered. Anyone can check it with the open-source verifier, without Mnestiq.

Two products

Open evidence. Professional detection and investigation.

Mnestiq recorder

The evidence format, recorder, verifier and a local dashboard. Free and open source, so you can audit it yourself.

  • An open spec and JSON Schema, aligned with OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions
  • Python SDK for Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible models
  • Signing keys held outside the agent, in Azure Key Vault or a dedicated signing service
  • Independent RFC 3161 timestamps and signed heartbeats
  • Crash-safe, size-capped, fails open by default
  • Dashboard runs on your machine only

Mnestiq Workbench

For security teams that need to see what their agents do as they run, and to investigate and prove what happened when something goes wrong.

  • Live detection: alerts in Microsoft Sentinel within minutes, every agent's activity, and a dashboard in the tools your SOC already uses
  • Agent evidence joined with flow, DNS, proxy, firewall and cloud logs, with a stated reason for every link
  • Microsoft Sentinel both ways: logs come into the case, triage decisions go back onto the incident
  • An independent Evidence Vault that catches evidence cut back or rewritten
  • Signed reports, and a claim pack written for insurers that anyone can check

Security model

What it proves, and what it doesn't.

Evidence is only useful if its limits are known. We state them plainly in the open spec and in a published threat model, where every attack considered is backed by an automated test.

Proves

Records weren't edited, deleted, inserted or reordered after they were written, given a pinned signing key.

Doesn't prove

That a compromised host told the truth when it wrote them. Corroborate with independent infrastructure logs. The Workbench does this.

Gap

On its own, an evidence file can be cut back to an earlier checkpoint without detection. Keep a copy of the latest checkpoint somewhere else and verify against it to close this. The Evidence Vault does this for you.

Keys

Signing keys can be held in Azure Key Vault or in a signing service under a separate account. A compromised agent cannot copy the key. With the signing service it also cannot have earlier evidence signed again, because the service signs each chain only forward. Key Vault signs whatever the agent's identity asks for, so there the Evidence Vault's copy is what shows a rewrite.

Verify, don't trust.

You should not have to take a security vendor's word for it. The recorder and its verifier are open source, every claim in the threat model is backed by an automated test, and any evidence file can be verified independently, without Mnestiq. Prompts and data stay on your own systems: only signed checkpoint fingerprints leave, and only to destinations you configure.

Independent review is welcome. The break-it challenge provides a signed, timestamped incident record: alter it without the verifier noticing, and tell us how.

Design partners

Running agents with real permissions in production? Let's talk.

We're looking for a small number of security and platform teams to shape the workbench around real incidents.

With the signing service it also cannot have earlier evidence signed again, because the service signs each chain only forward. Key Vault signs whatever the agent's identity asks for, so there the Evidence Vault's copy is what shows a rewrite.

content_html_zh:
Open source · forensic evidence for AI agents

Trace a network connection back to the AI agent step that made it.

Mnestiq records what your agents saw, decided and did as signed, tamper-evident evidence. When something goes wrong, you can name the run, the step, the input that drove it and who approved it, and prove the record wasn't altered afterwards.

pip install mnestiq

v1.1.1 · Apache-2.0 · Python 3.10+ · Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and compatible APIs · PyPI

One log line, tracedexample

  1. Firewall10.0.4.17:53120 → 198.51.100.9:25 · 48 KB · no agent identity
  2. Mnestiqagent support-bot · run f48cccfa · step 6 · sandbox container:a91f02 · operator acme-helpdesk
  3. Causeuntrusted input at step 4 (web, via fetch_page) → model requested send_email → approved by policy:email-auto-approve
  4. Evidencesealed by checkpoint · signer ed25519:6bec5262… (pinned) · corroborated by vpc-flow.log, conn.log

差距

Your logs see connections. Your traces see prompts. Nothing connects them.

A firewall alert: a host that runs AI agents sent 48 KB to an outside mail server on port 25. The responder now has three questions, and today's tools answer none of them.

Network logs

10.0.4.17:53120 → 198.51.100.9:25 · 48 KB

An address, a port and a byte count. No agent, run or step.

nothinglinks them

Agent traces

model call → tool call: send_email

Prompts and tool calls. No address, port or connection.

Q1

Which agent did this?

Firewall and flow logs show an IP and a port. They don't know about agents, runs or steps.

Q2

Why did it do it?

Was the instruction from the user, or from a web page, a document or another agent? That has to be captured when it happens, not reconstructed later.

Q3

Can we prove it?

Ordinary logs can be edited by anyone with write access. Evidence for a post-mortem, an insurer or a regulator needs to show it wasn't.

它是如何运作的

Record, verify, investigate.

01 · Record

A flight recorder in the agent

Records agents built on Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible models in a few lines. Built to fail safely: if recording fails, the agent keeps running.

  • Every piece of model input tagged by source: user, web, tool output, retrieved document, another agent
  • Tool calls, approvals and effective permissions
  • Every outbound connection, with run identity headers and the local address and port

usersystem webtool outputretrieved documentanother agent

Marked sources are treated as untrusted by the detection rules.

Quick startPython

# $ pip install "mnestiq[anthropic]"
# $ mnestiq keygen --out keys
# Instrument an existing agent. Your agent code doesn't change.
import anthropic
from mnestiq import FileSink, Recorder
from mnestiq.egress import instrument_egress
from mnestiq.integrations.anthropic import instrument_anthropic
from mnestiq.keys import load_private_key

recorder = Recorder(FileSink("evidence.jsonl"), agent_id="support-bot",
                    signing_key=load_private_key("keys/signing.key"))
client = instrument_anthropic(anthropic.Anthropic(), recorder)
instrument_egress()   # stamp and record outbound connections during runs

with recorder.run():
    ...                # your agent, as it is today
recorder.close()       # signs the last checkpoint: verify needs it

# Later: $ mnestiq verify evidence.jsonl --trusted-key keys/signing.pub

02 · Verify

Tamper-evident by construction

Records are hash-chained and sealed by Ed25519-signed Merkle checkpoints.

  • Edits, deletions, insertions and reordering fail verification
  • Pin the recorder's key, and a re-signed forgery is rejected
  • Redact prompts and customer data before sharing, and the proof still holds

recordhash of the record before

recordhash of the record before

recordhash of the record before

Signed checkpointMerkle root of the records it covers · Ed25519 signature

Change, remove, add or reorder a record and the hashes stop matching what was signed.

03 · Investigate

From a log line to a cause

Join agent evidence with the infrastructure logs you already collect.

  • VPC flow logs, Zeek and proxy logs linked to the exact agent step, with a confidence score
  • The untrusted input that preceded an action, and who approved it
  • Traffic from agent hosts that no recorded step explains

Every record above is sealed by a signed checkpoint.

When someone edits the record

Built for the person holding the incident.

What the responder gets

The run, the step, the input and the approval.

The same evidence file answers the three questions: which agent, why, and whether the record can be shown to be unaltered. Anyone can check it with the open-source verifier, without Mnestiq.

Two products

Open evidence. Professional detection and investigation.

Mnestiq recorder

The evidence format, recorder, verifier and a local dashboard. Free and open source, so you can audit it yourself.

  • An open spec and JSON Schema, aligned with OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions
  • Python SDK for Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible models
  • Signing keys held outside the agent, in Azure Key Vault or a dedicated signing service
  • Independent RFC 3161 timestamps and signed heartbeats
  • Crash-safe, size-capped, fails open by default
  • Dashboard runs on your machine only

Mnestiq Workbench

For security teams that need to see what their agents do as they run, and to investigate and prove what happened when something goes wrong.

  • Live detection: alerts in Microsoft Sentinel within minutes, every agent's activity, and a dashboard in the tools your SOC already uses
  • Agent evidence joined with flow, DNS, proxy, firewall and cloud logs, with a stated reason for every link
  • Microsoft Sentinel both ways: logs come into the case, triage decisions go back onto the incident
  • An independent Evidence Vault that catches evidence cut back or rewritten
  • Signed reports, and a claim pack written for insurers that anyone can check

安全模型

What it proves, and what it doesn't.

Evidence is only useful if its limits are known. We state them plainly in the open spec and in a published threat model, where every attack considered is backed by an automated test.

Proves

Records weren't edited, deleted, inserted or reordered after they were written, given a pinned signing key.

Doesn't prove

That a compromised host told the truth when it wrote them. Corroborate with independent infrastructure logs. The Workbench does this.

Gap

On its own, an evidence file can be cut back to an earlier checkpoint without detection. Keep a copy of the latest checkpoint somewhere else and verify against it to close this. The Evidence Vault does this for you.

Keys

Signing keys can be held in Azure Key Vault or in a signing service under a separate account. A compromised agent cannot copy the key. With the signing service it also cannot have earlier evidence signed again, because the service signs each chain only forward. Key Vault signs whatever the agent's identity asks for, so there the Evidence Vault's copy is what shows a rewrite.

Verify, don't trust.

You should not have to take a security vendor's word for it. The recorder and its verifier are open source, every claim in the threat model is backed by an automated test, and any evidence file can be verified independently, without Mnestiq. Prompts and data stay on your own systems: only signed checkpoint fingerprints leave, and only to destinations you configure.

Independent review is welcome. The break-it challenge provides a signed, timestamped incident record: alter it without the verifier noticing, and tell us how.
